stages.title: Advanced algebra
stages.hook: The equation x² + 1 = 0 has no real solution. Why would mathematicians invent a new kind of number just to solve it, and what can that number do?
explain: Polynomials are sums of powers of x with coefficients, like p(x) = x³ − 6x² + 11x − 6. The factor theorem says (x − a) is a factor of p(x) exactly when p(a) = 0. The remainder theorem says that dividing p(x) by (x − a) leaves remainder p(a). Here p(2) = 8 − 24 + 22 − 6 = 0, so (x − 2) is a factor; in fact p(x) = (x − 1)(x − 2)(x − 3).

For a quadratic ax² + bx + c = 0 the roots add to −b/a and multiply to c/a. For x² − 5x + 6 the roots 2 and 3 add to 5 and multiply to 6. Inequalities with modulus, such as |x − 3| < 2, mean x is within 2 of 3, so 1 < x < 5.

Complex numbers add i, defined by i² = −1, so that x² + 1 = 0 has solutions ±i. A complex number a + bi is added and multiplied like algebra with i² = −1: (2 + 3i)(1 − i) = 2 − 2i + 3i − 3i² = 5 + i. The modulus is |a + bi| = √(a² + b²), so |3 + 4i| = 5.

example.q: Find the remainder when p(x) = x³ + 2x − 5 is divided by (x − 2).
steps: By the remainder theorem the remainder is p(2).

analogies.music: Sound waves are combined using complex numbers to describe their phase.
analogies.city: Engineers factorise polynomials to find when a bridge model has zero stress.

misc.right: Complex numbers are used routinely in physics, signals and engineering; "imaginary" is just a historical name.

stages.title: Trigonometric functions and identities
stages.hook: A Ferris wheel turns steadily. Your height above the ground repeats every full turn. What function can describe that, and why do mathematicians use radians instead of degrees?
explain: On the unit circle (radius 1) an angle θ measured from the positive x-axis gives the point (cos θ, sin θ). So sin θ and cos θ are defined for every angle, not just those in right triangles. A radian is the angle for which the arc length equals the radius, so 180° = π radians and 360° = 2π. Radians make calculus formulas simple.

Graphs of sin and cos are waves with amplitude 1 and period 2π. The graph of y = A sin(bx) has amplitude A and period 2π ÷ b, so sin 2x has period π. Pythagoras on the unit circle gives the identity sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, and tan θ = sin θ ÷ cos θ.

The compound-angle and double-angle formulas are: sin(A + B) = sin A cos B + cos A sin B, sin 2θ = 2 sin θ cos θ and cos 2θ = cos²θ − sin²θ = 1 − 2 sin²θ. If sin θ = 3/5 for acute θ, then cos θ = 4/5, so sin 2θ = 24/25. Equations such as sin x = 1/2 have many solutions: 30° and 150° in one turn, and more by adding 360°.

example.q: If sin θ = 3/5 and θ is acute, find cos θ and sin 2θ.
steps: θ is acute so cos θ = 4/5.

stages.title: Exponential and logarithmic functions
stages.hook: A savings account grows by 5% each year. Why does it grow faster in later years than in earlier years, and how long until it doubles?
explain: An exponential function has the variable in the exponent: y = a × bˣ. If b > 1 it is growth, and if 0 < b < 1 it is decay. Growth of 5% a year means b = 1.05. After n years 1000 becomes 1000 × 1.05ⁿ, which is about 1 628.89 after 10 years. The growth in each year is proportional to the current amount, so it speeds up.

A logarithm is the inverse of an exponential: log_b y = x means bˣ = y. So log₂ 8 = 3 because 2³ = 8, and log₁₀ 1000 = 3. The laws are log a + log b = log(ab), log a − log b = log(a/b) and log(aⁿ) = n log a. These turn multiplication into addition and powers into multiplication.

To solve 2ˣ = 50 take logs of both sides: x log 2 = log 50, so x = log 50 ÷ log 2 ≈ 5.64. The number e ≈ 2.718 is the natural base for which the growth rate at each point equals the value, and ln means log base e. Many natural processes such as radioactive decay (half-life) are exponential.

example.q: A sum of 1 000 grows at 5% per year. Find the value after 10 years, to the nearest cent.

analogies.farm: A bacteria population in milk doubles every hour: 1, 2, 4, 8.
analogies.sea: Light fades exponentially with depth in the ocean.

analogies.city: A viral rumour spreads exponentially at first.

stages.title: Vectors and matrices
stages.hook: A plane flies at 200 km/h but the wind blows at 50 km/h from the side. How do you combine the two to find where the plane actually goes?
explain: A vector has both magnitude (size) and direction. We write it as a column, such as a = (3, 4). The magnitude is |a| = √(3² + 4²) = 5. Vectors add component by component: (3, 4) + (1, −2) = (4, 2). Multiplying by a scalar scales the vector: 3a = (9, 12).

The dot product of (a₁, a₂) and (b₁, b₂) is a₁b₁ + a₂b₂. For (2, 3) and (4, −1) it is 8 − 3 = 5. Also a · b = |a||b|cos θ, where θ is the angle between them, so vectors are perpendicular exactly when the dot product is 0: (1, 2) · (2, −1) = 0.

A matrix is a rectangular array of numbers. We multiply row by column: for A = [[1, 2], [3, 4]] and B = [[0, 1], [1, 0]], AB = [[2, 1], [4, 3]]. Matrix multiplication is not commutative: BA = [[3, 4], [1, 2]] is different. The determinant of [[a, b], [c, d]] is ad − bc, and a matrix has an inverse only if its determinant is not zero. A 2 × 2 matrix can transform the plane by rotating, stretching or reflecting.

example.q: Find the angle between a = (1, 0) and b = (1, 1).

stages.title: Limits and continuity
stages.hook: The expression (x² − 4)/(x − 2) is undefined when x = 2, yet its graph seems to head to a clear value there. What value, and what does it mean to "approach" a value?
explain: A limit describes what value a function approaches as the input approaches a point. We write lim (x→a) f(x) = L. The limit does not depend on what happens at x = a itself, only near it. For f(x) = (x² − 4)/(x − 2), cancelling the factor (x − 2) for x ≠ 2 gives x + 2, so the limit as x→2 is 4, though f(2) is undefined.

The limit exists when the left-hand and right-hand limits agree. If f(x) = x + 1 for x < 2 and 5 for x ≥ 2, the left limit at 2 is 3 and the right limit is 5, so there is a jump and no limit. Limits at infinity ask what happens for huge x: 1/x → 0, and (2x + 1)/x = 2 + 1/x → 2.

A function is continuous at a if the limit exists and equals f(a). Roughly, you can draw the graph without lifting the pen. Types of discontinuity are a removable hole, a jump and an infinite break (like 1/x at 0). Continuity is essential for calculus; the important limit lim (x→0) sin x / x = 1 (x in radians) leads to the derivative of sine.

steps: Direct substitution gives 0/0, which is undefined, so we simplify first.

analogies.sport: A sprinter's speed at an instant is the limit of average speed over shorter and shorter times.
analogies.tech: A digital zoom approaches the true value as the sampling gets finer.
analogies.nature: A cooling cup of tea approaches room temperature but never quite reaches it.
analogies.city: A car's speedometer shows the limit of distance over time for tiny time intervals.

A single missing point (a hole) that could be filled.

stages.title: Differential calculus
stages.hook: How can a car's speedometer tell you the speed at one exact instant, when speed seems to need a stretch of time to measure?
explain: The derivative measures the instantaneous rate of change. It is the gradient of the tangent to the curve. It is defined as a limit: f'(x) = lim (h→0) [f(x + h) − f(x)] / h. For f(x) = x² this gives (2xh + h²)/h = 2x + h → 2x.

Rules save work. The power rule says d/dx xⁿ = n xⁿ⁻¹, so d/dx (3x² + 2x) = 6x + 2. Also d/dx sin x = cos x and d/dx eˣ = eˣ. The chain rule handles functions inside functions: d/dx (3x + 1)² = 2(3x + 1) × 3 = 6(3x + 1). The product rule is (uv)' = u'v + uv'.

Where f'(x) = 0 the curve has a stationary point (maximum, minimum or inflection). For y = x² − 4x, y' = 2x − 4 = 0 gives x = 2 and y = −4, a minimum. Optimisation uses this: with perimeter 20 a rectangle x by (10 − x) has area x(10 − x), maximised when 10 − 2x = 0, so x = 5 and the area is 25.

example.q: Find the minimum value of y = x² − 4x.
steps: Set it to zero: 2x − 4 = 0 so x = 2.
Check it is a minimum: the second derivative is 2 > 0.

analogies.city: A factory chooses the production level where profit has a maximum, where its derivative is zero.
analogies.nature: The rate a population grows is the derivative of its size.
analogies.tech: A phone battery's discharge rate is the derivative of its charge.

misc.wrong: The derivative is the average speed over an interval.
misc.right: It is the instantaneous rate: the limit of average rates over shrinking intervals.

teach.model: The derivative tells you how fast something is changing at an exact moment. On a graph it is the slope of the tangent line at that point. For x² the derivative is 2x, so at x = 3 the slope is 6.

stages.title: Integral calculus
stages.hook: You know a car's speed at every moment. How can you work out how far it travelled? Is there a link between that and the area under the speed graph?
explain: Integration is the reverse of differentiation and also a way to find area. An indefinite integral gives an antiderivative: ∫ x² dx = x³/3 + C, where C is a constant, because many functions have the same derivative. The power rule is ∫ xⁿ dx = xⁿ⁺¹/(n + 1) + C for n ≠ −1.

A definite integral ∫ from a to b of f(x) dx gives the signed area between the curve and the x-axis. The fundamental theorem of calculus says it equals F(b) − F(a) where F is any antiderivative. For example ∫ from 0 to 3 of 2x dx = [x²] from 0 to 3 = 9 − 0 = 9, which is the area of a triangle with base 3 and height 6, namely 9.

Useful results: ∫ cos x dx = sin x + C, ∫ eˣ dx = eˣ + C and ∫ 1/x dx = ln|x| + C. Substitution reverses the chain rule: to find the integral from 0 to 1 of 2x(x² + 1) dx let u = x² + 1, so du = 2x dx and the integral is [u²/2] from u = 1 to u = 2 = (4 − 1)/2 = 1.5. If velocity is v = 2t, the displacement from t = 0 to 5 is ∫ 2t dt = 25.

example.q: Find the area under y = x² from x = 1 to x = 2.

analogies.sport: The total distance run is the area under the speed-time graph.
analogies.farm: Water filling a tank: the volume is the integral of the flow rate.
analogies.city: Total electricity used is the integral of power over time.

stages.mnemonic: Integrate: add one to the power and divide by the new power. Upper minus lower, area is the answer.
terms: The reverse of differentiation; also the area under a curve.
A function whose derivative is the given function.
An integral between limits that gives a number.
The + C in an indefinite integral.

misc.wrong: The integral always gives a positive area.
misc.right: Area below the axis counts as negative in a definite integral, so signed area can be zero.

trip.prompt: Find the diagram connecting area under a curve to antiderivatives.

questions.q: What is ∫ x² dx?
questions.why: Add 1 to the power and divide by the new power.

questions.q: If F'(x) = f(x), then ∫ from a to b of f(x) dx equals...
questions.why: This is the fundamental theorem of calculus.

questions.q: Why is + C needed in an indefinite integral?
o: Many functions differ by a constant and have the same derivative
questions.why: x² + 1 and x² + 5 both have derivative 2x.

questions.q: What is ∫ cos x dx?
questions.why: The derivative of sin x is cos x.

questions.q: A car's velocity-time graph is above the axis from 0 to 10 s. What does the area under it give?
o: The final acceleration of the car
questions.why: Velocity × time is distance.

questions.q: Lina says ∫ from −1 to 1 of x dx = 2 because it is the area under y = x. What is wrong?
o: Area below the axis counts as negative and cancels
questions.why: The integral is [x²/2] from −1 to 1 = 0.

questions.q: Find ∫ from 0 to 3 of 2x dx.
questions.why: [x²] from 0 to 3 = 9.

questions.q: Find ∫ from 1 to 2 of x² dx as a decimal to 2 decimal places.
A body has velocity v = 2t m/s. What is its displacement from t = 0 to t = 5 s in metres?
questions.why: [t²] from 0 to 5 = 25.

questions.q: Explain why the area under a curve can be found by an antiderivative.
questions.model: The rate of change of the area under a curve up to x equals the height of the curve at x. So the area function is an antiderivative of the curve: integration undoes differentiation.
questions.why: This is the key idea of the fundamental theorem of calculus.

panel.q: Evaluate ∫ from 0 to 1 of 2x(x² + 1) dx.
panel.why: Let u = x² + 1: ∫ from 1 to 2 of u du = (4 − 1)/2 = 1.5.

panel.q: The average value of f(x) = x² on [0, 3] is (1/3)∫ from 0 to 3 of x² dx. Calculate it and explain.
panel.model: ∫ from 0 to 3 of x² dx = 27/3 = 9. Dividing by the interval width 3 gives an average value of 3.
panel.why: The mean value is the area divided by the width.

panel.q: The speed of a runner is 4 m/s for 10 s and then 6 m/s for 5 s. What is the total distance?
panel.why: 4 × 10 + 6 × 5 = 70 m, the total area under the graph.

teach.model: Integration adds up many thin slices to find the total area under a curve. It is also the reverse of differentiation. To integrate x² you add one to the power and divide by it: x³/3. For a definite integral you plug in the top limit and subtract the bottom.

How do I get a number?

stages.title: Probability distributions
stages.hook: You guess every answer on a 5-question true/false quiz. How likely is it to get exactly 2 right, and how can one formula cover all such "repeat trial" situations?
explain: A random variable assigns a number to each outcome of a random process. A probability distribution lists the possible values and their probabilities. The expected value E(X) is the long-run average: for a fair die E(X) = (1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 6) ÷ 6 = 3.5.

The binomial distribution counts successes in n independent trials, each with success probability p. P(X = k) = C(n, k) pᵏ (1 − p)ⁿ⁻ᵏ, with mean np and variance np(1 − p). For 5 guesses with p = 0.5, P(X = 2) = 10 × (1/2)⁵ = 10/32 = 0.3125. For n = 10 and p = 0.3 the mean is 3 and the variance is 2.1.

The normal distribution is a continuous bell-shaped curve fully described by its mean μ and standard deviation σ. A z-score z = (x − μ)/σ tells how many standard deviations a value is from the mean: a mark of 70 when μ = 60 and σ = 5 gives z = 2. About 68%, 95% and 99.7% of values lie within 1, 2 and 3 standard deviations. For continuous distributions probability is area under the curve.

example.q: A fair coin is tossed 3 times. Find P(X = 0 heads) and P(at least one head).

analogies.sport: Number of goals in a match: a basketball player's free throws follow a binomial model with p equal to her success rate.
analogies.farm: The number of seeds out of 20 that sprout is binomial if each sprouts with the same chance.

stages.mnemonic: Binomial: count the successes in n trials. Normal: a bell, centred at the mean, width set by sigma.
terms: A numerical outcome of a random process.
The count of successes in n independent trials with probability p.
The number of standard deviations from the mean.

misc.wrong: The expected value is the value you expect to see on any single trial.
misc.right: E(X) = 3.5 for a die but you can never roll 3.5. It is a long-run average.

questions.q: For a fair die, E(X) is...
Which situation is binomial?
o: Number of heads in 10 tosses of a fair coin
Number of red cards in 5 cards dealt without replacement
Number of cards drawn until an ace appears
questions.why: Fixed n, independent trials, constant p, counting successes.

questions.q: The mean of a binomial with n = 10, p = 0.3 is...
questions.why: np = 3.

questions.q: A z-score of 2 means a value is...
questions.why: z = (x − μ)/σ.

questions.q: About what fraction of a normal distribution lies within 2 standard deviations of the mean?
A student says "the expected number of children is 2.4, so the family next door has 2.4 children." What is wrong?
o: Expected value is an average, not a value for one family
The expected value must be an integer
questions.why: The expected value is a long-run mean.

questions.q: For n = 3 fair coin tosses, find P(no heads).
For n = 5 and p = 0.5, find P(X = 2) as a decimal.
A mark is 70 with μ = 60 and σ = 5. Find the z-score.
Explain why P(at least one head in 3 tosses) is best found as 1 − P(no heads).
questions.model: At least one head includes 1, 2 or 3 heads, which is three cases to add. The complement (no heads) is a single case with probability 1/8, so 1 − 1/8 = 7/8.
questions.why: Using the complement avoids adding many cases.

panel.q: A game costs 1 to play. You win 10 with probability 0.1 and nothing otherwise (the 1 stake is kept by the host either way). What is your expected net gain?
panel.why: E(win) = 0.1 × 10 = 1, minus the 1 stake = 0.

panel.q: A normal distribution has mean 100 and standard deviation 15. Explain what percentage you expect between 85 and 115.
panel.model: 85 and 115 are 1 standard deviation (15) below and above the mean 100. About 68% of values lie within 1 standard deviation.
panel.why: Use the empirical rule.

panel.q: Why is P(X = exact value) equal to 0 for a continuous random variable such as height?
o: Probability is area under the curve, and a single point has zero width
panel.why: Only intervals have positive area.

teach.model: The binomial distribution counts how many successes you get in a fixed number of independent tries, when each try has the same chance of success. For example the number of heads in 5 coin tosses. You need the number of tries n and the chance p.

stages.title: Statistical inference and regression
stages.hook: A poll of 100 voters says 40% support a plan. How confident can you be that the whole population is near 40%? And does a trend line through some data prove one thing causes another?
explain: Statistical inference uses a sample to say something about a population. A sample statistic such as a mean varies from sample to sample. The standard error of a sample mean is σ/√n, so with σ = 10 and n = 25 it is 10/5 = 2. Larger samples give smaller standard error. For a proportion p̂ the standard error is √(p̂(1 − p̂)/n): for p̂ = 0.4 and n = 100 it is about 0.049.

A 95% confidence interval for a mean is roughly x̄ ± 1.96 × SE. If x̄ = 50 and SE = 2, the interval is 46.08 to 53.92. It means that the method produces intervals that capture the true value in 95% of repeated samples, not that there is a 95% chance this particular interval contains it. A hypothesis test asks whether data are consistent with a claim; the p-value is the probability of data at least this extreme if the claim (null hypothesis) were true.

Regression fits a line y = a + bx to paired data by least squares, minimising the sum of squared residuals (observed minus predicted). The correlation r (between −1 and 1) measures the strength of linear association, and r² is the share of variation explained. Correlation does not prove causation: a hidden factor may drive both variables.

example.q: Data (1, 2), (2, 3), (3, 5), (4, 6). Find the least-squares line and predict y at x = 5.
steps: Slope b = Σ(x − x̄)(y − ȳ) ÷ Σ(x − x̄)² = 7 ÷ 5 = 1.4.

analogies.city: Polls survey a few thousand voters to estimate the opinion of millions.
analogies.farm: Testing a sample of 30 plants to estimate the yield of a whole field.
analogies.sport: Fitting a line to training hours and race times, while knowing other factors matter.
analogies.tech: A company A/B tests two web page designs using a sample of visitors.

stages.mnemonic: Sample to population, with an error bar. A line through points is not a proof of cause.
terms: The standard deviation of a sample statistic, such as σ/√n for a mean.
A range built to capture the true value with a stated long-run success rate.
The probability of results at least this extreme if the null hypothesis is true.
Observed value minus the value predicted by the model.

misc.wrong: A 95% confidence interval means there is a 95% chance the true value is in this particular interval.
misc.right: The 95% refers to the method over many samples. Any one interval either contains the true value or not.

stages.limits: Regression lines should not be used far outside the range of the data (extrapolation), and a small p-value does not measure how large or important an effect is.

trip.prompt: Find the explanation of how many intervals from repeated samples capture the true mean.

questions.q: Which change makes the standard error of a mean smaller?
questions.why: SE = σ/√n.

questions.q: Two variables have r = 0.95. What can we say?
o: They have a strong positive linear association
questions.why: Correlation shows association, not cause.

questions.q: Ice cream sales and drowning numbers are positively correlated across months. The best explanation is...
o: The two series are measured in different units
A hidden factor such as hot weather
questions.why: Both increase in summer: a confounding variable.

questions.q: A residual is...
questions.why: Residuals measure how far points fall from the line.

questions.q: A small p-value (such as 0.01) suggests...
o: The null hypothesis is proved false
The data are unlikely if the null hypothesis were true
questions.why: It is evidence against the null, not proof, and says nothing about effect size.

questions.q: Aisha predicts a child's height at age 40 using a line fitted to ages 5 to 12. Why is this unreliable?
o: It extrapolates far beyond the data range
questions.why: The trend may not continue outside the observed range.

questions.q: σ = 10 and n = 25. Find the standard error of the sample mean.
x̄ = 50 and SE = 2. Find the upper end of the 95% interval x̄ ± 1.96 SE (to 2 d.p.).
Using y = 0.5 + 1.4x, predict y when x = 5.
Explain why a bigger sample gives a narrower confidence interval.
questions.model: The standard error is σ/√n, so a larger sample size n makes it smaller and the interval x̄ ± 1.96 SE narrower: more data means a more precise estimate.
questions.why: Precision grows with the square root of sample size.

panel.q: A poll finds 40% (SE about 4.9 points). Which statement is the best interpretation of the 95% interval of about 30% to 50%?
o: There is a 95% chance this interval holds the truth, so the truth is definitely in it
The poll is 95% accurate for every voter
The method captures the true proportion in about 95% of repeated polls
panel.why: Confidence refers to the long-run behaviour of the method.

panel.q: A study finds a correlation between hours of sleep and exam scores. Explain two reasons why this does not prove sleep causes better scores.
panel.model: A third factor such as general health or motivation could affect both, and the direction could be reversed. Only a well-designed randomised experiment can support a causal claim.
panel.why: Correlation shows association; cause needs experiments or other evidence.

panel.q: You test 20 unrelated things and one gives p = 0.04. What should you suspect?
o: It could be a chance finding from multiple testing
panel.why: With 20 tests at 5%, about one false positive is expected.

teach.topic: What a confidence interval tells you
teach.model: A confidence interval is a range of values that is likely to include the true population value, built from a sample. A 95% interval comes from a method that works 95% of the time over many samples. A bigger sample gives a narrower interval.
